source_text: Qui vero non hic, id est, non intra hunc ambitum terrae, nec per hunc commeatum vitae, nec apud homines hujus naturae communis confessionem putant constitutam, quanta praesumptio est adversus omnem ordinem rerum in terris istis, et in vita ista, et sub humanis potestatibus experiundarum? Nimirum cum animae de corporibus excesserint, et per singula tabulata coelorum de praecepto dispici coeperint, et interrogari arcana illa haereticorum sacramenta, tunc confitendum apud veras potestates et veros homines, Theletos scilicet et Abascantos et Acinetos Valentini. Nostrates enim, inquiunt, nec ipse Demiurgus constanter homines probabat veros esse, quos stillicidium situlae et pulverem areae et sputamen et locustas deputavit; etiam irrationalibus jumentis adaequavit. Plane ita scriptum. Non tamen idcirco aliud hominis genus intelligendum praeter nos: quos quia constat esse, et comparatione potuit induere, salva et proprietate generis, et singularitate. Neque enim si vita vitiata est, ut despectui judicata despectis compararetur, statim natura sublata est, ut alia in nomine ejus deputaretur. Atquin servatur natura, etsi suffunditur vita, nec alios novit Christus homines, quam de quibus dicit: Quem me aiunt esse homines? et: Quomodo vultis ut faciant vobis homines, et ita vos facite illis. Vide an servaverit genus, a quibus et testimonium sui exspectet, et in quos justitiae vicem mandat. Illos autem coelestes homines si expostulem mihi ostendi, facilius Aratus Persea, et Cephea, et Erigonam, et Ariadnam inter sidera deliniabit. Quis autem prohibuit Dominum illic etiam confessionem hominum faciendam manifeste determinare, ubi suam futuram aperte pronuntiavit? ut ita esset positum: «Qui in me confessus fuerit coram hominibus in coelis, et ego in illo confitebor coram Patre meo qui in coelis est?» Eripere me debuit ex isto terrenae confessionis errore, quam suscipi noluit, si coelestem praecepisset, quia nullos alios homines noveram praeter incolas terrae; ne ipso quidem adhuc tunc in coelis homine conspecto.
pass_a_gloss: But those who think that the confession is not established here, that is, not within this circle of the earth, nor through this journey of life, nor among men of this common nature, what a great presumption it is against all order of things on this earth and in this life and under human powers to be experienced? Doubtless when souls have gone out of bodies and have begun to be inspected by command through individual levels of the heavens and to be questioned about those secret sacraments of the heretics, then it must be confessed before the true powers and true men, namely Theletos and Abascantos and Acinetos of Valentinus. For our people, they say, not even the Demiurgus himself consistently approved men to be true, whom he assigned to be like the dripping of a bucket and the dust of the threshing floor and spittle and locusts; he also equated them with irrational beasts. It is written plainly thus. But not for this reason is another kind of man to be understood beyond us: whom because it is agreed that they exist and could have been used for comparison, with the property of the kind and the singularity preserved. For even if life is corrupted, so that it may be judged to be despised in comparison with the despised, the nature is not immediately abolished, so that another may be substituted in its name. But the nature is preserved, even if the life is corrupted, and Christ does not know other men than those about whom he says: Whom do men say that I am? and: How do you want men to do to you, and so you do to them. See if he preserved the kind, from whom he also expects testimony of himself, and in whom he commands the duty of justice. But if I were to ask to be shown those heavenly men, Aratus would more easily draw Perseus and Cepheus and Erigone and Ariadne among the stars. But who prevented the Lord from determining there also that the confession of men should be made manifest, where he openly declared that his own would be? So that it might be said: He who has confessed me before men, I will also confess him before my Father who is in heaven? He ought to have snatched me away from this error of earthly confession, which he did not want to receive, if he had commanded a heavenly one, because I knew no other men except the inhabitants of the earth; not even the man in heaven was seen by me at that time.

pass_b_english: But those who claim confession isn't established here—within this circle of earth, through this journey of life, among men of this common nature—what sheer presumption against every order of things on this earth, in this life, under human powers to be tested! Doubtless when souls exit their bodies and begin to be inspected by command through each level of the heavens, and those secret sacraments of the heretics are interrogated, then confession must be made before the true powers and true men—Theletos, Abascantos, and Acinetos of Valentinus. They say even the Demiurge himself didn't consistently judge our kind to be true men, since he likened them to a bucket's drip, threshing-floor dust, spittle, and locusts, even equating them with irrational beasts. It's written plainly enough. But that doesn't mean another kind of man exists beyond us—men whose existence is agreed on and who could serve for comparison while preserving both the kind's property and its singularity. Even if life is corrupted, so that it's judged despicable by comparison with the despicable, the nature isn't abolished so another can be substituted in its name. Nature is preserved, even when life is corrupted, and Christ knows no other men than those he speaks of: 'Who do men say that I am?' and 'However you want men to treat you, treat them the same way.' See if he didn't preserve the kind—from whom he expects testimony about himself and in whom he commands the duty of justice. But if I demanded those heavenly men be shown me, Aratus would more easily trace Perseus, Cepheus, Erigone, and Ariadne among the stars. Who prevented the Lord from determining right there that confession before men should be made manifest, where he openly declared his own future confession would be? So it would read: 'Whoever confesses me before men, I will also confess him before my Father who is in heaven?' He should have snatched me from this error of earthly confession, which he refused to accept, if he had commanded a heavenly one—since I knew no other men except earth's inhabitants; not even the man in heaven had been seen by me at that time.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A preserves the clause structure and nuances of the Latin (e.g., 'even if life is corrupted' for 'etsi suffunditur vita' [noting 'suffunditur' is likely an OCR error for 'vitiata' in the source, which the translator correctly handled based on the context and the provided text]). Pass B provides a fluent rendering without adding or contradicting the meaning. Scripture citations are correctly identified and integrated: 'Whom do men say that I am?' (Matthew 16:13/Mark 8:29) and 'How do you want men to do to you...' (Luke 6:31).
